Rick,

On Mar 6, 2007, at 1:28 PM, Rick Voland wrote:

> rJava does not compile in FreeBSD.  config.log is attached.  rJava  
> config sets incorrect paths for Java components.  Do I need to set  
> some environment variable?

The Java components seem to be ok. The config.log indicates that the  
Java needs some pthread-compatible library. I don't know what it was  
compiled with, but you should probably use something like:

PKG_LIBS=-pthread R CMD INSTALL ...

Alternative options may be -lpthread or some FreeBSD specific flags  
(I remember that FreeBSD used to have issues with threads as they  
were cooperative only, but it's been quite a few years that I had to  
deal with FreeBSD ...). If that doesn't work, you may also want to  
have a look a the Java libraries with ldd (or its BSD equivalent) to  
see what they were linked to.

Please let me know which solution works such that I can add a test to  
rJava for that.

Cheers,
Simon

Hey all,

Thanks for all the work on JRI and friends. I've got a bevvy of
questions which will follow starting with this one on the status and
aims of the project.

interface from uDig, a Java language Geographic Information System

        the user API is slightly different. It would be useful for our
        purposes to develop client code that worked equally well with
        the two approaches (apart, of course, for connection setup and
        tear down).

        equivalents to Rconnection:
                re.voidEval()
        which is not a necessary class but would be required to make
        sure a client built against one of the two systems would work
        against the other.

        For example, JRI's REXP has fields and constructors mixed up one
        after the other which makes the file impossible to read outside
        of an IDE and hard to read inside the IDE. Ideally the static
        fields would be made more compact for legibility, the seven
        instance fields would be grouped together, the constructors
        would be together... Is this something I could work on as I read
        the code? If so what kind of patches would you want (since I'm
        working from libs not from the svn source directly).


thanks for any comments,
adrian

It is not the only strategy, but it is the one that is safer for most  
users. With JRI you can build almost anything at a low-level, however  
that is not highly encouraged, because you have to have a profound  
knowledge of the R internals. But you can do it (also see the  
supplied JRI examples and JGR sources for some low-level construction  
of objects).

I agree that given the frequent use of data frames, it may be a good  
idea to write a wrapper at the Java level. However, a data frame in R  
is not just a simple list, so it would require some more interfacing  
(extra RDataFrame class etc.). Contributions are welcome, of course.

> Is this the current state of things in JRI? Alternatively, is there  
> example code for how to create lists, data.frames and S4 objects?
>

You don't really want to create S4 objects directly, that defies the  
whole point of OO encapsulation. You should use generators/constructors.

The rtest example shows how to build a data frame from scratch.

Cheers,

messages.subject: JRI cleanup and design
messages.body_plain:
Hey,

I'm slowly trying to understand JRI so I'm first hitting the things that
seem weird---strange layout of directories, mixed case in files. The
first questions are about that. The last question is to understand if we
can't separate more cleanly, on the Java side, the objects in the JVM
only and the objects pointing to R memory.


Layout:

What led you to the current directory layout? I ask because JRI seems
really different from other projects I'm used to and I vaguely remember
you saying that you didn't really do java. 

        Is there a reason *not* to put the .java files in org/rosuda/JRI
        which is where java people expect them?
        
        Is there a reason not to have all the source files in src, for
        example with
        src/java/org...
        src/c/*.c
        and so on. This would clean up the directories in an elegant
        way.

I just hacked the configure stuff and got it working after moving the
java files but I then broke everything trying to move the c files since
I have never tackled the autoconf/configure beast.

        Would you consider a re-structuring to a cleaner layout more
        recognizable by javaheads?

Also the java layout doesn't follow our expectations. For example, the
examples use the default package, have only two files but four classes,
and use lower case names for two of the packages which is legal but not
generally done.

        Would you consider moving the examples package to 
        src/java/org/rosdua/JRI/examples/
        and then have them define themselves in the package
        org.rosuda.JRI.examples?

Note, if we wanted to follow convention fully we would also move that
JRI to lower case. 



Files:

The files have some idiosyncrasies. Indentation is dominantly by spaces
but there are tabs mixed in as well. The comments sometimes run very
wide instead of sticking to something around 80/100 columns wide; as
Knuth showed with TeX, beyond that width things are hard to read. 

        Are you interested in patches or is everything up in the air
        right now because of your refactoring and not subject to
        collaboration?


Design:

This idea is not concrete yet in my mind but perhaps your experience
gives you a better understanding of this. I'm perplexed by a seeming
dual role of REXP where on the one hand it can be describing a pointer
to a structure in R memory and on the other hand it describes a pure
java structure which will eventually be assigned by the Rengine into the
R memory space. 

        Is this dual role necessary or could REXP be split into REXP
        which would point to an object in R memory and JRIEXP (or some
        other) which would be a pure Java construct?

The advantage would be to separate cleanly the construction of objects:
        JAVA -> JRI* -> Rengine => REXP
(where JRI* would take the place of RVector, RBoolean ...i.e JRIVector)
and their demolition
        REXP->JAVA objects

You've probably already covered this ground and have your reasons for
doing things your way. 


cheers,
  --adrian

not flow text ;).

Gérard,

rJava is compiling fine, it is JRI that is causing trouble and the  
reason is that JRI is compiled independently of R, so it's not using  
R's linker settings. A 'hot fix' is to edit rJava/jri/configure lines  
3329-3331 and replace

CPICF=-fPIC
JNISO=.so
JNILD="-shared ${JAVA_LIBS}"

by

CPICF=-KPIC
JNISO=.so
JNILD="-G ${JAVA_LIBS}"

I'll see if I can automate this by using R's settings for future  
releases ...

If you still run into trouble, you may also want to add -D_REENTRANT  
to CFLAGS and -lpthread (or analogous for your platform) to LDFLAGS  
if the Java you link to uses native threads.

Cheers,
Simon

You export the paths as normal user, but call R as root (with sudo). I
think the LD_LIBRARY_PATH variable isn't present for root when you set
it as normal user.

Please try something like this:

$ sudo -s
# export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=.:/usr/lib/R/bin:/usr/lib/R/lib:/usr/lib/jvm/java-1.5.0-sun-1.5.0.08/jre/lib/i386:/usr/lib/jvm/java-1.5.0-sun-1.5.0.08/jre/lib/i386/client
# R
> install.packages("JGR",dep=TRUE)
> q()
# exit
